title: One Registry to Rule them All - Sonny Merla, Mauro Luchetti, & Mattia Redaelli, Quantyca
talk_summary: They ship template GitHub repos (blueprints) with Docker, auth, cost tracking, and Langfuse observability baked in so teams only write business logic.

takeaways.technique: Per-use-case budget enforcement at the gateway
takeaways.what_they_do: The AI gateway holds a monthly/weekly budget per use case; usage erodes it and developers see remaining budget, so spend is attributed and capped centrally rather than per-agent guesswork.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can set in this AI gateway a budget... while the developers are using those budgets, it erodes, and it can brings to developers... the remaining part of those budgets

takeaways.technique: Private MCP registry with enterprise metadata
takeaways.evidence_quote: Each server has an owner... What are the environment... the authentication model... The cost attribution... the use case linkage

takeaways.technique: Golden-path blueprint repos with auth, cost tracking, observability pre-wired
takeaways.what_they_do: Two template repos (MCP and A2A) ship Dockerfiles, FastAPI scaffolding, auth, cost tracking, and Langfuse tracing so teams implement only business logic behind fixed interfaces/ports.
A use-case registry links each use case to its agents, MCP servers, and models, producing a lineage view so an outage in one component reveals all affected use cases.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the full lineage of the use case and also be able... to be sure... in case some parts of the lineage are affected by an outage or a problem and go back to the use case affected

takeaways.technique: Gateway-mediated tool calls with registry lookup
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents call MCP/A2A proxies through the AI gateway; the proxy looks up the real backend URL in the catalog and the agent authenticates with a separate header, centralizing auth and routing.
